chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isma'il ibn Jabir

A wind (puffiness/swelling) had befallen his face due to an ailment that struck him while he was in the state of Ihram. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The doctor who treats me prescribed for me a sa'ut (nasal drops) containing musk.' He said, 'Use it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use musk nasal drops while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the use of musk-based nasal drops (*sa'ut*) for a person in Ihram suffering from a facial ailment, clarifying that the prohibition on scent applies primarily to external application on the body rather than internal absorption through the nose. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the scent itself and the substance entering the body, allowing medicinal use of scented items without invalidating the state of consecration.
